inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 are competing fixes for the same problem (wallet rebroadcast leaking identity under -privatebroadcast): #34533 routes resubmission through private broadcast, #36330 suppresses resubmission entirely. They conflict in the same code path and need one decision; review #36330 (the narrower, no-new-machinery option) alongside #34533.

Rebroadcast cluster: #36398, #36482, #34533, #36330 and #36380 all modify ResubmitWalletTransactions/broadcast policy and will conflict. #36398 (only rebroadcast own transactions) is the broadest change and should be settled first, since it changes the behaviour the others restrict further; #36481 (manual rebroadcast RPC/GUI) is the mitigation for #36398's stated tradeoff that recipients must resubmit stuck incoming payments, so it should be reviewed in the same batch.

#35990 and #36886 both harden the read-only BDB parser against malformed files causing infinite loops during migration; #35990's visited-page tracking and bounds checks most likely subsume #36886's self-referencing-overflow-page case. Review #35990 first and check whether #36886 is still needed as a standalone.

Chain, order matters: #36442 (represent multipath in one Descriptor) then #36443 (reconstruct from expansion) then #36444 (store/export in wallet). All three were split across P2/P3 although only #36444 delivers the user-visible payoff; they are now one P3 chain.
Chain: #10102 (multiprocess) must land before #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect), which in turn feeds #19461.

Chain: #35918 (expose key expression parsing) is a declared dependency of #36885 (analyzedescriptor); #36070 and #36143 are sibling enablers of the same multisig wizard project (#35645) and benefit from being reviewed as a group.

Legacy-migration refactor chain: #34909 then #36823 then #36897. These move ~800 lines each and will force rebases on the migration bug fixes #34193, #36871 and #36825 — merge the fixes before the moves.
Silent payments: #32966 (receiving) precedes #35302 (sending, which also depends on #35301); do not review the sending half first.
#35433 and #36855 both open RPC deprecation cycles on wallet spend RPCs; one policy decision covers both and they should be reviewed together.

Coin-selection test PRs #36614, #36732, #36740, #36840, #36905 and the #36255 refactor all edit coinselection_tests.cpp / coinselector_tests.cpp and will conflict with each other; #36255 (the migration of CoinGrinder tests) should be sequenced first or last deliberately.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 core of fund-safety, migration-corruption and silent-data-loss bugs; a large P2 band of concrete wallet bugs, privacy leaks and major features; a long P3 tail of smaller fixes, enabling refactors and test coverage. The main cross-PR corrections were the rebroadcast/privacy cluster (four overlapping PRs that had been scattered across P1-P3), the multipath descriptor chain (enablers were banded above their own payoff), and internal refactors/test-coverage PRs that had been banded inconsistently against near-identical siblings.
